cards.prompt: Which fatty acid is anti-inflammatory, and which is pro-inflammatory when eaten in excess?
cards.answer: Omega-3 is anti-inflammatory; omega-6 is pro-inflammatory in excess.

cards.prompt: Your body can produce omega-3 and omega-6 on its own, so diet does not matter.
cards.answer: The body does not produce them; they must come from diet.

cards.prompt: The omega-3 component known for retina and brain health, essential for cognitive function, is ____.
Which omega-3 component is known as the anti-inflammatory one?
A friend eats lots of refined vegetable oils and processed snacks and wants healthier fats. What should they change in their omega intake?
cards.answer: Increase omega-3 and decrease omega-6, since refined oils and processed foods are heavy in omega-6.
cards.explanation: Omega-3 foods are rarer and costlier than omega-6 foods.

cards.prompt: Which is NOT a listed benefit of omega-3?
cards.answer: Omega-3 helps sleep, menstrual pain and skin; it does not raise omega-6.

cards.prompt: Compared with regular eggs, how much more DHA do omega-3 eggs contain?
cards.answer: Roughly 3-5x, or 100-150 mg or more extra DHA.
cards.explanation: EPA also rises, but not significantly.

cards.prompt: Omega-6 fats are rare in everyday food while omega-3 is everywhere.
cards.answer: It is the reverse: omega-6 is in many daily foods; omega-3 is rarer and pricier.
